questions.question: Which four fluids made up the body in humoral theory?
options: Blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile
questions.explanation: Blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile were thought to compose the body. Health was proportion among them.

questions.question: Which temperament was linked to yellow bile?
questions.explanation: Yellow bile is hot and dry, tied to summer and fire, and gives the choleric temperament.

questions.question: Which season and element went with phlegm?
questions.explanation: Phlegm is cold and wet, paired with winter and water. Winter coughs “pour phlegm.”

questions.question: Why did the humoral model last so long, according to the chapter?
options: Because microscopes seemed to confirm it
Because it was visible: anyone could see blood, mucus, and bile
questions.explanation: It lasted because it was visible. Anyone could see blood, mucus, and bile, and heat and cold were felt every feverish night.

questions.question: What did the theory get right by accident?
options: That four fluids are the whole physics of the body
That diet, season, sleep, and mood affect health
questions.explanation: Diet, season, sleep, and mood do affect health. The error was treating four fluids as the whole physics of the body.
